family_history.father: MI at age 62, died age 70 (stroke), HTN, DM2
family_history.siblings: Sister (age 52) - HTN; Brother (age 58) - DM2, CAD s/p stent

social_history.diet: High carb, fast food 3-4x/week, large portions

visits.chief_complaint: Annual physical exam, establishing new PCP after relocation
visits.hpi: 56 yo AAM presents for annual wellness visit. Recently moved to Chicago for work. Generally feels well. Notes occasional headaches, some fatigue. Wife encouraged visit due to family history of heart disease. Last physical 3 years ago. Takes no medications. Denies chest pain, SOB, edema.

physical_exam.heent: PERRL, EOMI, fundoscopic exam - mild AV nicking
physical_exam.cardiovascular: RRR, no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Normal S1/S2. No JVD.
physical_exam.neuro: Alert, oriented x3, CN II-XII intact, strength 5/5 throughout

medications_started: Aspirin 81mg daily (for primary prevention given risk factors)
counseling: Lifestyle modifications: DASH diet, reduce sodium <2300mg/day
Weight loss goal: 10-15 lbs over 6 months
Smoking cessation - praised for quitting, reinforced importance
preventive_care: Colonoscopy screening discussed - last done 2016, repeat due 2026
assessment_plan.follow_up: 2 weeks - BP recheck and lab review

ekg_results.interpretation: Normal sinus rhythm, rate 76, normal axis, no ST-T wave changes, no LVH

visits.subjective: Returns for lab review and BP recheck. Home BP readings averaging 142-148/88-94. Started DASH diet, reduced salt. Has not started exercise program yet. Feels well, no side effects from lisinopril.

plan: Increase lisinopril to 20mg daily
Start atorvastatin 40mg nightly (high-intensity statin for ASCVD >10%)
Prediabetes counseling - diabetes prevention program discussed
Goal: Lose 5-7% body weight (15 lbs) to prevent diabetes progression
Repeat lipids and HbA1c in 3 months
Continue home BP monitoring
Emphasize dietary changes and physical activity
assessment_plan.education: Discussed cardiovascular risk - combination of HTN, high cholesterol, prediabetes, family history puts him at high risk. Importance of medication adherence and lifestyle changes emphasized.

visits.subjective: Returns for BP check. Home readings improved, averaging 134-138/82-86. No side effects from medications. Started walking 20 min x 3-4 days/week. Diet improved but still struggling with portion control. No muscle pain from statin.

diagnoses: 1. Hypertension - improved but not at goal
plan: BP improved but still slightly above goal (<130/80)
Add hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) 12.5mg daily
Continue atorvastatin, lisinopril, aspirin
Praised for weight loss and exercise initiation
Encouraged to increase exercise to 30 min x 5 days/week
Consider referral to dietitian if difficulty with weight loss continues
assessment_plan.follow_up: 3 months - lab recheck (lipids, HbA1c), BP assessment

visits.subjective: Returns for lab review. Home BP readings at goal, averaging 128-132/78-82. Feeling well. Exercise routine maintained. Weight stable. No complaints.

diagnoses: 2. Hyperlipidemia - improved on statin (LDL reduced from 162 to 98)
plan: BP at goal - continue current regimen
LDL at goal (<100 for high ASCVD risk) - continue atorvastatin 40mg
HbA1c trending up (5.9% → 6.0%) - intensify diabetes prevention efforts
Weight loss stalled - referred to registered dietitian (nutrition counseling)
Consider metformin for diabetes prevention if HbA1c continues to rise
Repeat HbA1c in 6 months
referrals: Registered Dietitian - medical nutrition therapy for prediabetes and weight management

visits.subjective: Annual wellness visit. Generally feeling well. BP controlled on medications. Saw dietitian 2x - made some progress with diet. Exercise routine maintained but hasn't lost additional weight. Wife concerned about increased thirst and urination frequency over past 2 months. Pt attributes to drinking more water.

diagnoses: 3. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus - NEWLY DIAGNOSED based on symptoms and anticipated labs
orders: HbA1c, fasting glucose (STAT - symptoms concerning for DM)
plan: Polyuria/polydipsia concerning for diabetes - check labs today
Will call with results and likely start metformin
Continue current BP and cholesterol medications
If diabetes confirmed: referral to diabetes education, ophthalmology for diabetic retinal exam
Foot care education
assessment_plan.follow_up: Call with labs, then office visit in 1-2 weeks

visits.subjective: Returns after labs confirmed diabetes. HbA1c 7.8%, FBG 178. Pt shocked but not entirely surprised given family history. Willing to start treatment. Concerned about complications. Asking many questions about prognosis.

diagnoses: 2. Diabetic kidney disease, early stage (microalbuminuria present)
3. Hypertension - controlled (even more critical now with diabetes)
4. Hyperlipidemia - on statin (LDL goal now <70 given diabetes)
plan: Start metformin 500mg BID with meals (will titrate up)
Home glucose monitoring - fasting and 2-hour post-prandial
HbA1c goal <7%
BP goal <130/80 (diabetes present)
LDL goal <70 (diabetes = ASCVD equivalent) - increase atorvastatin to 80mg
ACE inhibitor (lisinopril) excellent for diabetic nephropathy - continue
Annual microalbumin monitoring
medications_started: Metformin 500mg BID (to be increased to 1000mg BID after 2 weeks if tolerated)
patient_education: Importance of glycemic control to prevent complications
assessment_plan.follow_up: 2 weeks - metformin tolerance check; then monthly until HbA1c at goal

visits.subjective: Returns for diabetes follow-up. Tolerating metformin well after initial GI upset - now on 1000mg BID. Checking blood sugars regularly - fasting 140-165, post-prandial 180-220. Completed DSME program - very helpful. Saw ophthalmology - mild NPDR noted (non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy). Trying to adhere to diabetic diet but finds it challenging. Thirst improved.

diagnoses: 1. Type 2 DM - inadequately controlled (home readings elevated)
plan: Blood sugars still above target (goal fasting <130, post-meal <180)
Increase metformin to maximum dose: 1000mg with breakfast, 1000mg with dinner
Check HbA1c in 6-8 weeks
If HbA1c not improved, will need to add second agent (likely GLP-1 RA or SGLT2i)
Continue aggressive BP and lipid control
Ophthalmology follow-up in 6-12 months per their recommendation

visits.subjective: Returns for HbA1c check. Home glucose logs show improvement: fasting 125-145, post-prandial 160-190. Weight down 4 lbs. Exercise increased to 5 days/week. Diet adherence better. No hypoglycemic episodes. No medication side effects.

diagnoses: 1. Type 2 DM - improved but not at goal (HbA1c 7.2%)
plan: HbA1c improved (7.8% → 7.2%) but not at goal <7%
Need additional medication
Discussed options: DPP-4 inhibitor, GLP-1 RA, SGLT2i, insulin
Given kidney disease, chose SGLT2 inhibitor for renal protective effects
Start empagliflozin (Jardiance) 10mg daily
Educated about genital yeast infections, UTI risk, euglycemic DKA (rare)
Continue metformin 1000mg BID
Repeat HbA1c in 3 months
assessment_plan.counseling: Explained SGLT2 inhibitor mechanism - helps kidneys excrete glucose, promotes weight loss, protects kidneys and heart. Important to stay well-hydrated.

visits.subjective: Returns for comprehensive follow-up. Feeling very well. Glucose control much better - fasting 110-125, post-prandial 140-165. Energy improved. Weight down. No medication side effects. Exercising regularly. Diet adherence good.

diagnoses: 5. Obesity - improving (lost 13 lbs, BMI decreased from 31.5 to 29.6)
plan: Excellent progress! HbA1c at goal, LDL at goal, BP controlled, weight loss achieved
Continue all current medications
Maintain current lifestyle modifications
Monitor HbA1c every 6 months while stable
Continue annual diabetic eye exams, annual kidney monitoring
Discussed potential for further weight loss - close to overweight (not obese) category
assessment_plan.patient_education: Congratulated patient on excellent lifestyle changes and medication adherence. Explained importance of maintaining these habits long-term. Discussed diabetes as chronic condition requiring ongoing management.
assessment_plan.follow_up: 6 months - routine diabetes follow-up, HbA1c recheck

visits.subjective: Returns for routine diabetes follow-up. Continues to do well. Blood sugars stable - fasting 105-120, post-prandial 135-160. Weight maintained. Exercise routine established - walks 5 days/week, joined gym. No new complaints. Recent eye exam - stable mild NPDR. Podiatry visit - no foot issues.

diagnoses: 2. History of diabetic nephropathy - RESOLVED (microalbumin normalized)
plan: Outstanding diabetes management - HbA1c 6.5%, kidney function improved, microalbumin normalized
Lost 16 lbs total since diagnosis, nearly to normal BMI
Continue all medications - current regimen very effective
Discussed long-term outlook - with continued good control, risk of complications very low
Next HbA1c in 6 months
Continue annual comprehensive diabetes care (eyes, feet, kidneys)
Updated immunizations - flu vaccine given
assessment_plan.counseling: Praised patient for exceptional commitment to health. Discussed that this is a model case of how diabetes can be successfully managed with combination of medications and lifestyle changes. Encouraged to maintain current habits.

problem_list.complications: Mild NPDR (non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy), history of microalbuminuria (now resolved)

problem_list.note: Was obese (BMI 31.5) at diagnosis, lost 16 lbs

immunizations.pneumococcal: PPSV23 given Sept 2021, PCV20 due at age 65

clinical_pearls: Classic progression from prediabetes to diabetes with polyuria/polydipsia symptoms
Strong family history of diabetes, cardiovascular disease - high-risk patient
African American male with HTN and DM - higher risk for kidney disease
Excellent example of successful chronic disease management with medications + lifestyle
Multi-drug regimen necessary: metformin + SGLT2i for diabetes, ACE + thiazide for BP, high-intensity statin for CV risk
SGLT2 inhibitor choice driven by renal protective effects given early nephropathy
Microalbuminuria normalized with good glucose control and ACE inhibitor - demonstrates reversibility of early diabetic kidney disease
notes.risk_factors: High 10-year ASCVD risk (18.2%), family history of premature CAD, African American race (higher DM/HTN complications), former smoker
